extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students interested in engineering history and practical self-education (readers of George Stephenson biography)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria describe the habits, practices, and practical principles exemplified by George Stephenson for becoming a successful mechanic/engineer and inventor—covering self-education, hands-on practice, troubleshooting, prototyping, and communication. Useful as a rubric for evaluating or guiding practical mechanical engineering apprenticeship and inventive practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use spare moments for learning and earning
rubrics_metrics.description: Every spare moment was laid under contribution by him, either for the purpose of adding to his earnings, or to his knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: working evenings and nights mending shoes, cleaning clocks and watches, making shoe-lasts, cutting out clothes, and building models; convert idle time into incremental skill- and capital-building activities. Anti-pattern: letting spare time go unproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master machinery by disassembly and hands-on study
rubrics_metrics.description: It continued to be his regular habit, on Saturdays, to take his engine to pieces, for the purpose, at the same time, of familiarising himself with its action, and of placing it in a state of thorough working order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice: routinely take machines apart and reassemble them to learn details of action and maintenance. Benefit: enables turning knowledge to practical account and rapid diagnosis of faults. Scoring note: frequency and depth of hands-on teardown work indicate strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnose root causes and apply principled mechanical remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: He observed that the ropes ... became worn out ... finding it to be occasioned by excessive friction, he proceeded ... to shift the pulley-wheels and re-arrange the gearing, which had the effect of greatly diminishing the tear and wear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle: identify the underlying cause (e.g., friction, flow restriction) and alter system geometry or arrangement to reduce wear. Example: enlarging an injection cock, raising cistern, re-arranging pulley geometry. Anti-pattern: superficial fixes that ignore root cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test and iterate boldly (including departures from received directions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stephenson ... determined to work [the boiler] at a pressure of ten pounds, though this was contrary to the directions of both Newcomen and Smeaton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: where justified by observation and testing, experiment with parameters beyond conventional prescriptions, but observe effects and adjust accordingly. Scoring note: measured risk-taking backed by empirical results is valued; reckless, unmonitored departures are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriately sized prototypes to solve local problems
rubrics_metrics.description: He said, 'he would set up for them an engine little bigger than a kail-pot, that would clear them out in a week.' And he did so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build small, fit-for-purpose engines/models to address specific tasks (scaled prototypes). Example: little engine to pump out ochre quarry. Benefit: fast, low-cost practical validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study prior art and scientific literature to avoid wasted effort
rubrics_metrics.description: He afterwards used to lament the time he had lost in these futile efforts, and said that if he had enjoyed the opportunity ... of learning from books what previous experimenters had accomplished, he would have been spared much labour and mortification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: read foundational texts (e.g., Ferguson's Lectures) and journals to learn what is already known; reduces reinventing known fallacies (e.g., perpetual motion). Anti-pattern: solitary, uninformed reinvention leading to wasted labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine practical tinkering with theoretical rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: In these evening entertainments, the mechanical contrivances were supplied by Stephenson, whilst Wigham found the scientific rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: pair hands-on model-building with theoretical explanation—either via collaboration or self-study—so that experiments are informed by scientific principles. Example: testing specific gravities using simple devices and interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop competence in arithmetic, mensuration, and reading drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: He made much progress in the higher branches of arithmetic ... Wigham taught him to draw plans and sections ... 'A good plan should always explain itself;' and, placing a drawing of an engine or machine before the youth, would say, 'There, now, describe that to me--the arrangement and the action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: acquire mathematical skills (rule of three, mensuration) and the ability to read and produce plans/sections; practice describing arrangements and action from drawings without text. Scoring: fluency in interpreting and communicating drawings is a key capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate perseverance and patient practice
rubrics_metrics.description: So much patient perseverance could not but eventually succeed; and by dint of practice and study, Stephenson was enabled to master successively the various rules of arithmetic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: steady, sustained practice (e.g., repeated arithmetic exercises, chalk calculations on waggons) leads to mastery; value long-term persistence over short bursts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise personal discipline and temperance
rubrics_metrics.description: He continued a sober man. ... he made a dead stop, and said, firmly, 'No, sir, you must excuse me; I have made a resolution to drink no more at this time of day.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: maintain steady habits and self-restraint; personal discipline supports reliability and professional reputation. Anti-pattern: intemperance leading to loss of character and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and manage a trusted, cohesive work team
rubrics_metrics.description: The only condition that he made, before setting to work, was that he should select his own workmen. ... 'The workmen,' said he, 'must either be all Whigs or all Tories.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: insistence on choosing one's own team to avoid internal friction and jealousy; pragmatic team selection to ensure cooperation. Note: the specific political phrasing reflects historical context; principle is about ensuring team cohesion and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate and teach others—spread practical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes he would endeavour to impart to his fellow-workmen the results of his scientific reading ... his son Robert also early endeavoured to communicate to others the information which he had gathered at school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: share discoveries and methods with peers and apprentices; teaching deepens understanding and raises community capability. Example: Robert teaching algebra to pitmen's boys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design plans and documentation to be self-explanatory
rubrics_metrics.description: 'A good plan should always explain itself;' and, placing a drawing ... would say, 'There, now, describe that to me--the arrangement and the action.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: create drawings and plans that clearly convey arrangement and function without heavy reliance on text; favor clarity and legibility in technical documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply ingenuity to small practical problems and domestic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: He won the women's admiration by connecting their cradles with the smoke-jack, and making them self-acting. ... He also contrived a wonderful lamp which burned under water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: inventive talent is demonstrated by solving everyday problems with clever mechanical adaptations; such small-scale innovations build reputation and practical skills.
